coverage: Evening edition, Mon Nov 23 (covers the Fri Nov 20 close, the weekend and the Thanksgiving week ahead)
moodReason: The S&P 500 fell 8.6% in the week of Nov 16 to 20, its worst week since April 2025, as AI and chip stocks sold off. Futures pricing now gives about 91% odds of a December rate hike, and the week ahead is dominated by October core PCE inflation.

stories.headline: AI and chip stocks drive the S&P 500 into correction and its worst week since April 2025
stories.what: The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% on Friday Nov 20 and the S&P 500 fell 3.7%, with the Dow down 1.9%. For the week the S&P 500 lost 8.6%, the Dow about 8% and the Nasdaq about 10%. Nvidia fell about 14% on Friday, and the VIX closed at its highest level since April 2025.
stories.why: Tech and chip stocks carry a large share of index weight, so their selloff drags the whole market down. Investors are also questioning whether heavy AI spending will earn enough profit to justify current valuations.

stories.headline: Futures put about 91% odds on a December Fed rate hike, with some officials pushing for a bigger move
stories.what: Fed funds futures priced roughly 91% odds of a quarter-point hike at the Dec 8 to 9 meeting as of Nov 22. Governor Waller has floated a half-point hike in December, a larger move that markets had not priced in. Minutes from the October meeting showed nearly all officials expect to raise rates next month.
stories.why: Higher expected rates raise borrowing costs and lower the present value of future earnings, which hits high-valuation growth stocks hardest. Small caps, which borrow heavily, are also sensitive, and the Russell 2000 fell 2.8% on Nov 20.

stories.headline: October core PCE inflation and Q3 GDP revision land Wednesday, the last major data before the Fed's blackout
stories.what: October core PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, is due Wednesday Nov 25, with forecasts clustering around 3.2% year over year. Q3 GDP is revised the same day, and some economists expect growth to be revised up to about 3.6% from the advance estimate of 3.4%. The Fed's pre-meeting quiet period starts Saturday Nov 28.
stories.why: A hot PCE print would strengthen the case for a December hike and could push yields and tech stocks lower. A soft print would ease pressure, though one analysis notes it would not cancel a hike.

stories.headline: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut fails to revive the AI trade as investors take profits
stories.what: Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq in a record IPO, but the AI rally did not carry over. Investors took profits in AI names after the debut, and the selloff in AI and chip stocks deepened through Friday.
stories.why: A weak debut after a record IPO was read as a sign of limits to investor appetite for AI valuations. Amazon and Alphabet hold stakes in Anthropic, so their shares are linked to its trading.

stories.headline: Dell earnings Tuesday will test whether AI server demand is holding up
stories.what: Dell reports Tuesday Nov 24, and investors will focus on its AI order backlog, AI-server margins and guidance. Nvidia already reported on Nov 17, but its shares fell sharply in the following days.
stories.why: Strong AI orders would ease fears that AI spending is slowing, while weak backlog or margins would add to the selloff in AI hardware names.

bottomLine: US stocks end a painful week with the S&P 500 down 8.6% and the Nasdaq down about 10%, led by AI and chip stocks. Futures put about 91% odds on a December Fed hike, so the market now treats higher rates as the base case rather than a risk. The holiday-shortened week hinges on Wednesday's October PCE print, and that data will set the tone into the Dec 8 to 9 Fed meeting.
